q.label: Semaglutide (Ozempic, Rybelsus, Wegovy) and sudden vision loss (NAION)
q.hook: Europe and the UK now warn that semaglutide can, very rarely, cause sudden vision loss. The U.S. label doesn't.

EU.finding: PRAC concluded June 2025 that NAION is a very rare side effect of semaglutide; SmPC sections 4.4 and 4.8 updated with warning, frequency very rare, ~2-fold increased risk (~1 extra case per 10,000 person-years).

UK.finding: MHRA Drug Safety Update February 2026 agreed with EU recommendations to update product information despite noting conflicting evidence; 3 Yellow Card reports; SmPC/PIL updates pending.

US_label.finding: Current US labels for Ozempic, Wegovy, and Rybelsus contain no mention of NAION, non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, or related optic neuropathy terms in any section.

US_regulator.finding: FDA AEMS Q4 2024 lists NAION as a potential signal for the GLP-1 receptor agonist class including semaglutide products (Ozempic, Rybelsus, Wegovy); FDA is evaluating the need for regulatory action.

hypotheses.name: different_evidence_bases_reviewed
hypotheses.why: EU reviewed large epidemiological studies and clinical trials; UK added spontaneous reports and noted conflicting evidence; FDA evaluating FAERS data for entire GLP-1 class.

hypotheses.name: class_effect_vs_single_product_assessment
hypotheses.why: EU and UK assessed semaglutide products specifically; FDA AEMS lists NAION as potential signal for the entire GLP-1 receptor agonist class.

hypotheses.name: divergent_causality_thresholds
hypotheses.why: EU PRAC deemed evidence sufficient for 'very rare' SmPC warning; UK agreed despite noting conflicting evidence; FDA requires higher certainty before label change, still evaluating.

hypotheses.name: signal_detection_timing_differences
hypotheses.why: FDA AEMS signal detection Q4 2024 preceded EU PRAC conclusion June 2025 and UK DSU February 2026, but EU acted first on regulatory decision.

hypotheses.name: risk_benefit_interpretation_variance
hypotheses.why: EU concluded NAION risk warrants SmPC warning given benefit-risk; UK concurred; FDA has not determined evidence sufficient to alter labeling.

why.sentence: The main reason is divergent causality thresholds, because EU PRAC deemed epidemiological evidence sufficient for a 'very rare' SmPC warning while FDA requires a higher evidentiary bar for label changes and is still evaluating class-wide FAERS data.

reasons.claim: EU concluded and updated SmPC; UK agreed and will update; US label silent and FDA evaluating.
EU used epidemiological studies and trials; UK added spontaneous reports and noted conflicts; FDA uses FAERS class-wide data.
EU and UK assessed semaglutide specifically; FDA evaluating entire GLP-1 receptor agonist class.

evidence.note: EU relied on several large epidemiological studies and clinical trial data showing ~2-fold increased risk; UK referenced the EU review plus 3 spontaneous Yellow Card reports and explicitly noted conflicting evidence; FDA is evaluating spontaneous reports (FAERS) for the entire GLP-1 receptor agonist class.

recommendation.reason: EU and UK have concluded NAION warrants a product warning; US label lacks any mention; hospital dispenses US semaglutide products to 75 patients who should be counseled on sudden vision changes.

hypotheses.name: class_effect_vs_single_product_assessment
hypotheses.why: EU and UK assessed semaglutide-specific risk, leading to product-specific label updates (EU-SMPC-OZEMPIC-01, UK-DSU-2026-02-05-01); US FDA evaluates NAION as a class effect across GLP-1 RAs (AEMS-Q42024-Non_arteritic_anterior_i, SENTINEL-NAION-GLP1), which may delay product-specific regulatory action.

hypotheses.name: divergent_causality_thresholds

hypotheses.name: signal_detection_timing_differences

hypotheses.name: risk_benefit_interpretation_variance
hypotheses.why: EU and UK concluded that the evidence warrants product information updates despite conflicting data (EU-SMPC-OZEMPIC-01, UK-DSU-2026-02-05-01), whereas US FDA continues evaluation without regulatory action, indicating a different risk-benefit threshold for label changes.

evidence.note: EU relied on spontaneous reports (EudraVigilance), literature, social media, and MAH cumulative reviews; UK reviewed literature since 2019; US sertraline label covers only treatment-emergent sexual dysfunction; fluoxetine label notes persistence in Adverse Reactions; FDA FAERS/AEMS and Sentinel show no listed signal.

recommendation.reason: The US sertraline label does not warn about persistent sexual dysfunction after stopping (related_only only), while EU and UK have concluded regulatory actions; an in-house reminder and counseling at next dispensing is warranted.

q.label: Darolutamide (Nubeqa) and angioedema
q.hook: In June 2026 PRAC recommended adding angioedema to darolutamide's EU product information (the company then has two months to apply for the change).

EU.finding: PRAC recommended update of EU product information to add angioedema to SmPC section 4.8 with frequency 'Not known' based on spontaneous post-marketing reports (June 2026).

UK.finding: No MHRA Drug Safety Update mentions darolutamide or androgen receptor inhibitors with angioedema.

US_label.finding: US label (Nubeqa v24, effective 2026-09-28) lists angioedema (includes laryngeal edema, lip swelling, swelling face, swollen tongue) in section 6.2 Postmarketing Experience only.

US_regulator.finding: FDA AEMS quarterly potential signal lists (2023 Q1–2026 Q2) contain no entry for darolutamide or androgen receptor inhibitors with angioedema.

hypotheses.name: eu_signal_triggered_by_eu_cases
hypotheses.why: Cannot confirm EU signal based solely on EudraVigilance cases not mirrored in FAERS; US label already includes angioedema, FDA signal lists show no entry.

hypotheses.name: us_label_already_includes_angioedema
hypotheses.why: US label (v24, 2026-09-28) already lists angioedema in section 6.2 Postmarketing Experience, which may explain lack of separate FDA signal action.

hypotheses.name: uk_mhra_awaiting_more_evidence
hypotheses.why: MHRA Drug Safety Updates search found no mention of darolutamide angioedema; no evidence of pending review or issued warning.

hypotheses.name: class_effect_assessment_differs
hypotheses.why: PRAC recommendation is specific to darolutamide; no reference to class effect across androgen receptor inhibitors.

hypotheses.name: different_causality_assessment
hypotheses.why: PRAC recommendation cites spontaneous reports and recommends label update without stating causal relationship confirmed; US label similarly includes in postmarketing.

hypotheses.name: timing_difference_us_uk_pending
hypotheses.why: FDA potential signal lists (2023-2026) show no darolutamide/angioedema entry; MHRA search shows no scheduled review.

why.sentence: The main reason is different regulatory stage: EU concluded a formal signal assessment requiring SmPC update, while US label already lists angioedema in postmarketing but FDA has not issued a signal action.

reasons.claim: EU completed a formal PRAC signal assessment (June 2026) mandating SmPC section 4.8 update; US label includes angioedema only in postmarketing section with no FDA signal list entry.

evidence.note: Both EU and US assessments rely on spontaneous post-marketing reports; PRAC cites spontaneous reports, US label cites postmarketing experience. No controlled trials or observational studies cited. The evidence is considered limited to spontaneous reporting.

recommendation.reason: EU has formally added angioedema to SmPC undesirable effects with 'Not known' frequency; US label includes it only in postmarketing section, so an in-house reminder at dispensing is warranted.

reopen_when.text: FDA adds angioedema to Warnings and Precautions (section 5) or Boxed Warning of darolutamide label.

state.askedText: The EU lists it only as an undesirable effect (SmPC 4.8) and the U.S. label lists it outside the warnings too: the two labels say it at the same level. A new in-house reminder needs a reason beyond a label difference; otherwise recommend already covered or no action. The draft cites a U.S. label version from the last year that mentions the reaction, yet the U.S. FDA cell says no public action. The FDA approves every label version: either change the FDA stage to concluded (the label was updated) and say which version added it, or, if the label's mention is not this reaction, change the U.S. label status to not found. Ruled out with no record against it: H4 class effect assessment differs, H5 different causality assessment, H6 timing difference us uk pending. Put the records that rule it out under "against". 1 explanations hold but none is named the main cause. Name exactly one main cause and say why it weighs more than the others. Revise: (1) Change recommendation to 'already_covered' or 'no_action' because EU SmPC 4.8 and US section 6.2 are equivalent non-warning sections. (2) Update US_regulator stage to 'concluded' citing the label version that added angioedema. (3) Move the ruling-out records for H4, H5, H6 from 'for' to 'against'. (4) Designate H2 as the main cause in the why chain and explain why it outweighs the open hypotheses.

q.reaction: DRESS (drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms)
q.label: Gemcitabine and DRESS
q.hook: In June 2026 PRAC recommended adding DRESS to the EU product information of gemcitabine medicines (the companies then have two months to apply for the change).

EU.finding: PRAC recommended updating EU product information (SmPC sections 4.4 and 4.8) to include DRESS as part of SCARs warning for gemcitabine (June 2026).

UK.finding: No MHRA Drug Safety Update mentions gemcitabine-DRESS signal.

US_label.finding: US label (Gemcitabine Hospira v28, effective 2026-04-27) includes DRESS in Warnings and Precautions 5.3 (SCARs including DRESS), Postmarketing 6.2, and Patient Counseling 17.

US_regulator.finding: FDA AEMS potential signals list (Q3 2023) identified DRESS signal for gemcitabine; FDA updated labeling May-Sep 2024 to include SCARs (including DRESS) in Warnings and Precautions, Adverse Reactions, Patient Counseling.

hypotheses.name: different_evidence_base
hypotheses.why: No case-count data from EudraVigilance, FAERS, or Yellow Card provided to compare.

hypotheses.name: different_causality_assessment
hypotheses.why: FDA also found sufficient evidence to update labeling for SCARs (including DRESS) in 2024.

hypotheses.name: different_regulatory_threshold
hypotheses.why: US label was updated in 2024 to include SCARs with DRESS named; not unchanged.

hypotheses.name: class_effect_vs_single_drug
hypotheses.why: All regulators focus on gemcitabine alone; no class-wide extension in evidence.

hypotheses.name: timing_of_review
hypotheses.why: PRAC June 2026 recommendation is newer than FDA's Q3 2023 signal list and 2024 label update.

why.sentence: The main reason is timing_of_review, because the PRAC's June 2026 recommendation for a DRESS-specific SmPC update is newer than the FDA's 2024 label update for SCARs broadly and the Q3 2023 signal list.

reasons.claim: EU PRAC recommendation (June 2026) is a newer review than FDA's 2024 label update and Q3 2023 signal list.

evidence.note: Regulators relied on spontaneous reports (EudraVigilance, FAERS) and postmarketing cases; PRAC cited sufficient evidence for label change, FDA updated label for SCARs class including DRESS, MHRA has no public assessment.

recommendation.reason: The US label already warns about DRESS in Warnings and Precautions (SCARs including DRESS), Postmarketing, and Patient Counseling, so current dispensing counseling covers the risk.

reopen_when.text: If FDA adds a boxed warning or revises the SCARs warning to emphasize DRESS specifically.
If FDA's quarterly signal list shows a new or upgraded DRESS signal for gemcitabine.

q.reaction: neurodevelopmental disorders in children of fathers treated with valproate
q.label: Valproate taken by fathers and neurodevelopmental disorders in their children
q.hook: Since 2024 Europe and the UK have told men taking valproate to use contraception, because of a possible risk to their children. In June 2026 PRAC re-reviewed newer, mixed studies: it kept those measures and asked for the product information to say the evidence is inconsistent.
q.note: first EU action January 2024 (CMDh endorsed PRAC's precautionary measures), UK Drug Safety Update 5 September 2024; the June 2026 PRAC entry in the night-scan ledger is a re-review

EU.finding: EU PRAC recommended precautionary measures for male valproate patients (contraception counseling, 3-month wait after stopping) in January 2024 based on a retrospective observational study suggesting possible increased NDD risk; in June 2026 PRAC reaffirmed measures despite inconsistent evidence.

UK.finding: UK MHRA issued a Drug Safety Update in September 2024 advising healthcare professionals to inform male patients of possible NDD risk and recommend effective contraception during treatment and 3 months after, based on the same observational study.

US_label.finding: US Depakote label (v1621, 2026-03-31) contains a boxed warning for neurodevelopmental disorders after in utero (maternal) exposure and mentions adverse reproductive effects in males from animal studies only (section 8.3), not human paternal exposure NDD risk.

US_regulator.finding: FDA quarterly potential signal lists (2023 Q1–2026 Q2) contain no entry for valproate paternal exposure and neurodevelopmental disorders; no label update or public communication on this risk.

hypotheses.name: eu_precautionary_principle_lower_threshold

why.sentence: The main reason is that EU and UK regulators have concluded precautionary measures based on a single observational study, whereas US FDA has not yet identified a signal or updated labeling.

reasons.claim: EU and UK have concluded precautionary regulatory actions while US FDA has not publicly acted on this signal.

evidence.note: EU and UK relied on a retrospective observational study using Nordic registry data (PASS) suggesting a possible increased NDD risk (cumulative risk 4.0–5.6% vs 2.3–3.2%), but noted limitations and inconsistent findings from other studies; US FDA has no public evaluation.

q.hook: Since 2024 Europe and the UK have told men taking valproate to use contraception, because of a possible risk to their children. In June 2026 PRAC re-reviewed newer, mixed studies: it kept those measures and asked for the product information to say the evidence is inconsistent.

EU.finding: EU PRAC recommended precautionary measures for male patients in 2024 (contraception, counseling) and maintained them in 2026 after reviewing inconsistent evidence from the PASS study and other studies.

UK.finding: UK MHRA issued a Drug Safety Update in September 2024 advising contraception and counseling for men on valproate based on the same retrospective observational study (PASS) reviewed by EU PRAC.

US_label.finding: Depakote U.S. label (v1621, 2026-03-31) warns of neurodevelopmental disorders following in utero exposure (Section 4, 5.1) and notes adverse reproductive effects in males from animal studies (Section 8.3), but does not mention neurodevelopmental disorders in children of fathers.

US_regulator.finding: FDA quarterly potential signal lists (2023 Q1–2026 Q2) show no signal for valproate paternal exposure neurodevelopmental disorders; no label update, drug safety communication, or other public action found.

why.sentence: The main reason is that the FDA has not yet evaluated the paternal valproate exposure signal, leaving the U.S. label without a warning, while the EU and UK have implemented precautionary measures.

q.reaction: neurodevelopmental disorders in children of fathers treated with valproate
q.label: Valproate taken by fathers and neurodevelopmental disorders in their children
q.hook: Since 2024 Europe and the UK have told men taking valproate to use contraception, because of a possible risk to their children. In June 2026 PRAC re-reviewed newer, mixed studies: it kept those measures and asked for the product information to say the evidence is inconsistent.
q.note: first EU action January 2024 (CMDh endorsed PRAC's precautionary measures), UK Drug Safety Update 5 September 2024; the June 2026 PRAC entry in the night-scan ledger is a re-review

EU.finding: EU PRAC recommended precautionary measures for male patients in 2024 (contraception, counseling) and maintained them in 2026 after reviewing inconsistent evidence from the PASS study and other studies.

UK.finding: UK MHRA issued a Drug Safety Update in September 2024 advising contraception and counseling for men on valproate based on the same retrospective observational study (PASS) reviewed by EU PRAC.

US_label.finding: Depakote U.S. label (v1621, 2026-03-31) warns of neurodevelopmental disorders following in utero exposure (Section 4, 5.1) and notes adverse reproductive effects in males from animal studies (Section 8.3), but does not mention neurodevelopmental disorders in children of fathers.

US_regulator.finding: FDA quarterly potential signal lists (2023 Q1–2026 Q2) show no signal for valproate paternal exposure neurodevelopmental disorders; no label update, drug safety communication, or other public action found.

hypotheses.why: EU and UK both reference the same PASS study; no newer data unique to EU.

hypotheses.name: uk_mhra_aligned_but_not_yet_published
hypotheses.why: UK MHRA published Drug Safety Update in September 2024 with precautionary advice.

hypotheses.name: us_fda_awaiting_sentinel_or_faers_confirmation
hypotheses.why: FDA potential signal lists show no entry for paternal valproate exposure; no label update or communication found. No record indicates FDA is awaiting Sentinel/FAERS confirmation; this hypothesis remains open.

hypotheses.name: us_label_already_contains_class_warning
hypotheses.why: US label warns only of in utero exposure neurodevelopmental disorders and animal male reproductive effects, not paternal exposure neurodevelopmental disorders.

hypotheses.name: eu_precautionary_principle_lower_threshold
hypotheses.why: UK took similar precautionary measures, so difference is not EU vs UK but EU/UK vs US.

why.sentence: The main reason is that the FDA has not yet evaluated the paternal valproate exposure signal, leaving the U.S. label without a warning, while the EU and UK have implemented precautionary measures.

reasons.claim: FDA has not publicly evaluated the paternal exposure signal, while EU/UK have concluded precautionary actions.

evidence.note: EU and UK relied on a retrospective observational study (PASS) using Nordic registry data, which suggested a possible increased risk but had limitations; other studies did not confirm the risk. PRAC considered evidence inconsistent and causal role uncertain. US FDA has not publicly reviewed this evidence.

recommendation.reason: US label lacks paternal-exposure warning; EU/UK have precautionary measures. Committee should wait for FDA label update or signal evaluation before proposing in-house counseling, as hospital currently dispenses no valproate.

q.reaction: neurodevelopmental disorders in children of fathers treated with valproate
q.label: Valproate taken by fathers and neurodevelopmental disorders in their children
q.hook: Since 2024 Europe and the UK have told men taking valproate to use contraception, because of a possible risk to their children. In June 2026 PRAC re-reviewed newer, mixed studies: it kept those measures and asked for the product information to say the evidence is inconsistent.
q.note: first EU action January 2024 (CMDh endorsed PRAC's precautionary measures), UK Drug Safety Update 5 September 2024; the June 2026 PRAC entry in the night-scan ledger is a re-review

EU.finding: EU PRAC recommended precautionary measures for male patients in 2024 (contraception, counseling) and maintained them in 2026 after reviewing inconsistent evidence from the PASS study and other studies.

UK.finding: UK MHRA issued a Drug Safety Update in September 2024 advising contraception and counseling for men on valproate based on the same retrospective observational study (PASS) reviewed by EU PRAC.

US_label.finding: Depakote U.S. label (v1621, 2026-03-31) warns of neurodevelopmental disorders following in utero exposure (Section 4, 5.1) and notes adverse reproductive effects in males from animal studies (Section 8.3), but does not mention neurodevelopmental disorders in children of fathers; the cited sections do not refer to paternal exposure.

US_regulator.finding: FDA quarterly potential signal lists (2023 Q1–2026 Q2) show no signal for valproate paternal exposure neurodevelopmental disorders.

why.sentence: The main reason is that the FDA has not evaluated the paternal valproate exposure signal, leaving the U.S. label without a warning, while the EU and UK have implemented precautionary measures.

reasons.claim: FDA has not publicly evaluated the paternal exposure signal, while EU/UK have concluded precautionary actions.

evidence.note: EU and UK relied on a retrospective observational study (PASS) using Nordic registry data, which suggested a possible increased risk but had limitations; other studies did not confirm the risk. PRAC considered evidence inconsistent and causal role uncertain. US FDA has not publicly reviewed this evidence.

recommendation.reason: US label lacks paternal-exposure warning; EU/UK have precautionary measures. Committee should wait for FDA label update or signal evaluation before proposing in-house counseling, as hospital currently dispenses no valproate.

items.title: Trintellix U.S. label v18 (effective 2025-03-05)
items.section: 12 CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY > 12.2 Pharmacodynamics > SPL UNCLASSIFIED SECTION
items.text: Effect on Cardiac Repolarization The effect of vortioxetine 10 mg and 40 mg administered once daily on QTc interval was evaluated in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-, and active-controlled (moxifloxacin 400 mg), four-treatment-arm parallel study in 340 male subjects. In the study the upper bound of the one-sided 95% confidence interval for the QTc was below 10 ms, the threshold for regulatory concern. The oral dose of 40 mg is sufficient to assess the effect of metabolic inhibition.

items.title: Trintellix U.S. label v18 (effective 2025-03-05)
items.text: Vortioxetine pharmacological activity is due to the parent drug. The pharmacokinetics of vortioxetine (2.5 mg to 60 mg) are linear and dose-proportional when vortioxetine is administered once daily. The mean terminal half-life is approximately 66 hours, and steady-state plasma concentrations are typically achieved within two weeks of dosing.

q.reaction: Hallucinations, not related to serotoninergic syndrome
q.label: Vortioxetine (Trintellix) and Hallucinations, not related to serotoninergic syndrome

EU.finding: EU PRAC recommended updating product information for vortioxetine to include hallucinations not related to serotonin syndrome (June 2025).

UK.finding: No MHRA Drug Safety Update or other public action found for vortioxetine hallucinations unrelated to serotonin syndrome.

US_label.finding: US label (v18, March 2025) does not list hallucinations unrelated to serotonin syndrome in warnings, contraindications, adverse reactions, or patient counseling; cited sections (Contraindications 4, Adverse Reactions 6, Patient Counseling 17) address serotonin syndrome but not hallucinations as a separate non-serotonin-syndrome reaction. Section 5 (Warnings and Precautions) was not provided in the records, so its content cannot be confirmed.

US_regulator.finding: FDA AEMS quarterly potential signal lists (2023 Q1-2026 Q2) contain no signal for vortioxetine hallucinations.

hypotheses.name: different_evidence_base
hypotheses.why: EU PRAC reviewed a post-marketing signal for vortioxetine hallucinations not related to serotonin syndrome (PRAC-R170); US FDA and MHRA have no public record of such signal review, but absence of evidence is not evidence of absence, so this remains open.

hypotheses.name: different_causality_threshold
hypotheses.why: No records available to compare causality thresholds across regulators.

hypotheses.name: different_class_effect_scope
hypotheses.why: EU signal is specific to vortioxetine (PRAC-R170), while US label only addresses serotonin syndrome (SPL-Trintellix-v18-4-76zm, SPL-Trintellix-v18-6-ptsr, SPL-Trintellix-v18-17-1pgq). This describes a difference in scope but does not explain why the regulatory divergence occurred.

hypotheses.name: different_regulatory_timing
hypotheses.why: EU PRAC recommendation (June 2025) is newer than last US label update (March 2025); US/UK may adopt similar warning in future cycle.

hypotheses.name: different_serotonin_syndrome_differentiation
hypotheses.why: The EU's differentiation of hallucinations from serotonin syndrome describes a labeling difference observed between regions, but does not explain why the regulatory divergence occurred; it restates the difference rather than identifying a cause.

why.sentence: The main reason is different regulatory timing: the EU PRAC recommendation (June 2025) postdates the last US label update (March 2025), so the US may adopt a similar warning in a future cycle; a secondary reason is different class effect scope, as the EU signal is specific to vortioxetine while the US label only addresses serotonin syndrome.

reasons.claim: EU PRAC recommendation (June 2025) postdates the last US label update (March 2025), so US/UK may adopt similar warning in a future cycle.
EU signal is specific to vortioxetine (PRAC-R170), while US label only addresses serotonin syndrome (SPL-Trintellix-v18-4-76zm, SPL-Trintellix-v18-6-ptsr, SPL-Trintellix-v18-17-1pgq).

evidence.note: EU PRAC recommendation based on signal detection from post-marketing spontaneous reports; US FDA has no public signal or label update for this reaction; no MHRA public action found.

recommendation.reason: EU PRAC recommends product information update for hallucinations not related to serotonin syndrome; US label lacks this warning, so in-house counseling is warranted for 20 patients on vortioxetine.

reopen_when.text: US label adds hallucinations not related to serotonin syndrome in Warnings and Precautions or Boxed Warning
